columns.rationale: Tail number has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 3322 equal to the table's row_count 3322, making it a complete unique identifier; samples like N10156 and N102UW follow the FAA registration pattern.

Landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but all samples are integral year values (min 1956.0, max 2013.0), justifying a cast to INTEGER; null_rate 0.021072 (70 nulls) means the manufacture year is unknown for a small share of aircraft, so nulls are retained.
Aircraft type has null_rate 0.0 and only 3 distinct values (Fixed wing multi engine, Fixed wing single engine, Rotorcraft), a clean complete categorical column.
Manufacturer has null_rate 0.0 and 35 distinct values; samples such as AIRBUS, BOEING, and BELL are plain uppercase manufacturer names needing no transformation.
Model has null_rate 0.0 and 127 distinct values; samples like 172N and 421C mix digits and letters, so it stays VARCHAR as landed.
Landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but the full distinct_values list is {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}, all integral with null_rate 0.0, so the engine count casts safely to INTEGER.
Landed as DECIMAL(38,9) with null_rate 0.0; all samples (2.0 through 12.0) and the min 2.0 and max 450.0 are integral seat counts, supporting a cast to INTEGER.

Landed as DECIMAL(38,9); all 13 distinct values (90.0 through 432.0) are integral, so it casts to INTEGER, but null_rate 0.993076 (3299 nulls) means the column is very sparsely populated and nulls are retained rather than imputed.
Engine type has null_rate 0.0 and 6 distinct values (4 Cycle, Reciprocating, Turbo-fan, Turbo-jet, Turbo-prop, Turbo-shaft), a complete clean categorical column.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata true; a capture-tool record id (3322 distinct UUIDs) with no business meaning, dropped per policy.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata true; a single constant extraction timestamp (2026-09-02T23:26:22) from the capture tool, dropped per policy.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata true; a single constant value of {} carrying no information, dropped per policy.

decisions.rationale: tailnum has distinct_count 3322 equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so one row per aircraft tail number is the evidenced grain.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across 3322 rows, so no deduplication step is applied.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata and carry no business content (the extraction timestamp is a single constant and _airbyte_meta is always {}).
year, engines, seats, and speed landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but every profiled sample and distinct value is integral, so all four are cast to INTEGER.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 nulls of 3322 rows) but the 13 populated distinct values are valid cruise speeds, so the column is retained nullable rather than dropped or imputed.
year has 70 nulls (null_rate 0.021072); the manufacture year is simply unknown for those aircraft, so nulls are retained without imputation.

purpose: silver_nyc_planes is the cleaned aircraft dimension derived from bronze.nyc_planes: one row per registered aircraft (tailnum) with its type, manufacturer, model, engine configuration, seat count, manufacture year, and cruise speed. It feeds flight-level analyses that join on tail number.
usage: Join to flight tables on tailnum, which is unique and never null. Numeric attributes (year, engines, seats, speed) are plain INTEGER after casting from the landed DECIMAL(38,9). Consumers using year must handle nulls (about 2.1% of rows), and consumers using speed must deliberately account for it being null on roughly 99.3% of rows.
limitations: Cleanup is schema- and type-level only: no imputation was performed, so the 70 null year values and the 3299 null speed values (null_rate 0.993076) remain null. Pipeline metadata columns from the capture tool were dropped, so source-extraction lineage is not carried in silver. Grain uniqueness on tailnum is evidenced by the profile (3322 distinct of 3322 rows) but must be confirmed against the warehouse before approval.
